shortcut.title: Title of the dialog that lists keyboard shortcuts.
shortcut.groups: Headings that group the shortcuts in the dialog.
shortcut.labels: Names of actions that have a keyboard shortcut. They also appear in the command palette and in tooltips.
shortcut.labels.aiGenerate: AI is a feature name that needs the user to provide an API key.
shortcut.tabRange: {{prefix}} is the modifier keys, for example "Alt+". Result: "Alt+1 to 9".
shortcut.unassigned: Shown when an action has no key combination.
shortcut.change: Button that starts recording a new key combination.
shortcut.clear: Button that removes the key combination of an action.
shortcut.reset: Button that returns an action to its default key combination.
shortcut.replace: Button that takes a key combination away from the action that uses it now and gives it to this one.
shortcut.capturing: Shown while the app waits for the user to press the new keys.
shortcut.captureHint: Escape is the key name and stays in English.
shortcut.customised: Badge on shortcuts the user changed.
shortcut.conflict: {{chord}} is a key combination such as Ctrl+K, {{label}} is the name of the action that uses it.
shortcut.moving.title: Heading of the list of navigation keys that cannot be changed.
shortcut.moving.typing: Shown instead of a key for actions that start when the user types letters.
shortcut.moving.labels: Explanations of the fixed navigation keys. The collection tree is the list of requests in the sidebar.
shortcut.moving.labels.leaveEditor: In code editors Tab inserts a tab character, so this explains how to leave the editor with the keyboard. Esc and Tab are key names.
shortcut.webNotice: Shown in the web app only. Alt, Ctrl, Shift and the key names stay as written.
shortcut.errors: Reasons why a key combination cannot be used.
shortcut.errors.altGraph: AltGr is a key on some keyboards that types symbols.
shortcut.errors.metaUnsupported: The Windows or Super key is the key with the operating system logo.
